findings.description: Bar A's functional check yielded an unasked-for law. The covariance channel amplifies the reciprocal's relative error by K/(1-K): P' = (1-K)*P, so a relative error d in K becomes d*K/(1-K) in (1-K). Measured at P=10, R=1: amplification 10.00, observed P relative error 0.1167 against resid*amp = 0.1172, ratio 1.00. This is the application-side gain that the iterative composition theorem calls L (MonitorSoundness.lean:118), appearing in RTL rather than in a hypothesis. As K -> 1 - a confident measurement, P >> R - the amplification diverges. The theorem said the contraction constant belongs to the surrounding system; this is the surrounding system handing over its constant.

Bar D's framing partly dissolved, in the same species as bar 1. The bar asked which BIST replaces the exhaustive sweep, which presupposes the BIST still owns coverage. Under the two-instrument doctrine it does not: the BIST's job is IDENTITY, not coverage. Identity needs a witness that is deterministic, pre-committed and sensitive to datapath change - not an exhaustive one. Coverage belongs to the monitor, and the monitor reaches territory no sweep could, since bar 4's texture finding showed the good set beyond the certified domain has no interval structure. So "representative, not exhaustive" is not a concession here; it is the correct specification, and chip 1's exhaustiveness was over-provision forced by having only one instrument. Recommendation: species (i) pre-committed trajectory ROM; species (ii) REJECTED rather than deferred, because it is exhaustive over the step function - already the most trusted part, dominated by the byte-identical reciprocal - and structurally cannot exercise the recursion, which is what chip 2 adds.

chip/synth/recip.ys sets NO parameters, so it synthesises eml_reciprocal at the module defaults WIDTH=32, FRAC=16 and reports 227,174 um2 - roughly 3.4x the true 16/8 figure. That is the project's own named prior defect (defaulting the kernel's parameters, which previously read a latency of 16 where the truth is 17) sitting unnoticed inside a committed measurement script. Found only because chip 2's whole design measured SMALLER than its own sub-component, which is impossible and forced the check. A baseline that is 3.4x wrong would have made any chip-2 area comparison meaningless in the flattering direction.

Bar A measured. 6x2 fits at 60.1% utilisation with all nine setup corners positive and DRC/antenna/violations zero. Rule 22's triple reported together: Yosys 80,853.80 um2, placed standard-cell 135,595 um2, utilisation 0.600505. 4x2 would require 90.9%, above the 85% at which SWEEP_002 observed this flow fail - stated as an inference from two observations, not a measurement. The stdcell field was identified by matching chip 1's known 121,031 rather than by reading its name; design__instance__area is the CORE area and would have overstated by 67%.

The area curve finally has three points, five runs after WORST_PATH_DIAGNOSIS_001.md:104 asked for them, and the prediction that produced the request is FALSIFIED. Ratios: 1.677 at 60.1% utilisation, 1.691 at 70.9%, 1.680 at 81.1% - a 0.8% spread. The record expected the constant to vary with utilisation pressure because repair-buffer count grows as packing tightens; repair-buffer share is 11.0% versus 10.2%, so the named mechanism is real but nearly flat over this range. The third point cost one local Yosys run: chip 1's full submitted design had never had its Yosys area recorded, so its 81.1% point had no ratio at all. Validity conditions recorded per rule 22, including the one that limits it most: all three points are dominated by the same reciprocal, so the constant may be design-specific rather than flow-general, and nothing tests above 0.81.
